metadata.title: Broadcom stock sinks. Are AI earnings expectations 'insatiable'?

content.text:
Broadcom (AVGO) stock sinks further in Thursday trading despite topping estimates for fiscal second quarter earnings and revenue, while also outpacing forecasts on third quarter guidance.
Northwestern Mutual Wealth Management Company CIO Brent Schutte joins Yahoo Finance Senior Reporters Ines Ferré and Brooke DiPalma in assessing Broadcom's post-earnings stock reaction compared to other AI players.
its biggest fall in on record for this stock. Um and that is because of the AI chip uh revenue outlook for the third quarter that came in shy of expectations. Um that came in below expectations and this is something that some Wall Street analysts have been noting. Now, keep in mind Saz, this stock was priced for perfection. I mean, we saw it at intraday highs yesterday before it sold off in the last few minutes of of of the uh trading session.
And it had gained at one point 300 billion in market cap uh over the last five sessions. So, analysts had already been anticipating that that if this was not stellar and if they did not raise their guidance, then you would see a sell-off. And that is what we're seeing. The question now is, is this the start of a bigger sell-off in the semiconductor space or rotation out of this space.
heading into this report over the past month, Dell, HPE, Cisco, all these companies seeing major returns. I mean, taking a look at their stock prices following their reports. You have HPE up about 93% of the past month. You have Dell up 100%, Cisco up 40%, Snowflake up 70%. And over the past month alone for Broadcom, uh we did see now down 2%, but year to date, this stock was up 17% as Inez noted, this was really priced for perfection. And if this w w w uh rot continues throughout the day, I mean, the amount of uh market cap from a market cap perspective that Broadcom is expected to lose will be among the worst that we've seen on Wall Street, only surpassed by Microsoft earlier this year, Nvidia in early 2025. I mean, this will be quite a significant pullback for Broadcom.
Well, you hear this word insatiable thrown out around quite a bit. And the thing that I've noticed in my 31 years of doing this is when that word gets thrown around, someone in in a capitalistic society is figuring out how to satiate that demand and that usually brings down prices. And so that would be the first point. Pay attention to the sustainability of these earnings because I know there is some earnings behind these companies that people point to, but that's where can they continue. Two, you took me down memory lane, Cisco, Dell, Hewlett Packard, all the old names that I used to buy in my 31 years of doing this.
This is where AI is moving through the value chain of bringing it to life. We've gone from chips to hyperscalers, to memory, to data centers, to AI servers. And that's why I would encourage investors to think more about the longer-term benefits, which will be more towards the broader uh equity market where the companies that use AI to increase the profitability and productivity are going to be the ones that benefit. And this is where that narrow market of the late 1990s turned into a much broader market because companies used the .com or the internet um more broadly uh to bring their profits up. And that's why I encourage people to continue thinking about not trying to figure out where it goes next, but kind of remain overly or remain diversified so that you can pick it up uh as it moves through the rest of the value chain.
